summary: Frontend retest at 375x667 (mobile). AUTH ✓ (login padre.test@timeguard.dev / Familia123 succeeds and session persists). Dashboard now renders without the 'Falta preparar Supabase' error panel — the previous drift on `devices.name` and `extra_time_requests.minutes` IS resolved and SELECT works (returns 200/empty array). Tabs (tab-resumen, tab-actividad, tab-controles, tab-ajustes) all mount and switch. Sign out from Ajustes returns to auth-email. HOWEVER, the FOCUS FEATURE (extra_time_requests) is completely blocked because the `devices` INSERT still fails: `pairing-generate` returns HTTP 400 (Supabase code 23502 – NOT NULL violations on legacy columns `device_name`, `device_type`, `device_uuid` that were NEVER dropped when the new columns were added). Therefore: 0 devices are created → no `block-<id>` rows appear → `simulate-request` button is not rendered (the code hides it when devices.length === 0) → extra_time_requests approve/deny/persist flow CANNOT be exercised through the UI. Auth + tab navigation + sign-out work; pairing/block/requests are gated by the devices schema drift described below.

critical.issue: HTTP 400, code 23502: 'null value in column "device_name" of relation "devices" violates not-null constraint'. After supplying device_name, next failure is column `device_type` (NOT NULL + CHECK constraint), then `device_uuid` (NOT NULL). These legacy columns from a prior migration were not removed when the new columns (name, profile_name, platform, online, blocked) were ALTER-added. The app's insert payload {family_id, name, profile_name, platform, pairing_code} therefore always violates NOT NULL. Reproduced with real user JWT.

minor.issue: Table has BOTH the legacy column set (device_name, device_type, device_uuid, ...) and the new column set (name, profile_name, platform, online, blocked). SELECT works because it only reads the new columns, but any INSERT from the app cannot succeed.

integration_issues.issue: Pressing pairing-generate calls supabase.from('devices').insert(...) which returns 400 (see backend_issues). The modal stays open, pairing-code stays as '------', no DeviceRow appears, no Alert is shown to the user (error is only logged to console).

Because devices.length === 0 (insert blocked upstream), the simulate-request button is conditionally not rendered — `{devices.length > 0 && <Pressable testID="simulate-request" .../>}`. So the pending → approved (APROBADA) / denied (DENEGADA) flow, the badge counter, and persistence-after-reload could NOT be exercised end-to-end. Once the devices INSERT is fixed this flow needs a rerun.
Not testable while devices INSERT is broken (no block-<id> switch is rendered).

issues: The 'DISPOSITIVOS' Stat label wraps to two lines on a 375px viewport (visible in screenshot). Consider shortening to 'DISPOS.' or reducing font-size for that label.

action_items: Audit public.extra_time_requests the same way — legacy NOT NULL columns may still exist there too (SELECT of minutes/reason/status works, but INSERT was never verified because devices was blocked). Recommended: attempt an INSERT with minutes/reason/device_id only; if 23502 comes back, DROP the offending legacy columns or DROP TABLE + recreate.

In /app/frontend/app/index.tsx `addDevice` and `createRequest` show Alert only for the returned error object; the current failure is silent because those handlers succeed at the JS layer (result.error is set but the Alert.alert on line 71 does fire — actually it DOES call Alert; but on web the Alert shows as a native browser prompt/console log so it wasn't visible in the modal). Consider surfacing a persistent inline error message inside the Pairing modal instead of relying on Alert.alert (which is web-hostile).

Make /app/supabase/schema.sql idempotent at COLUMN level (not just table level) so repeated runs converge: after each `create table if not exists`, add matching `alter table … add column if not exists …` for every declared column AND `drop column if exists …` for known legacy names.
After the schema is fixed, rerun this iteration to exercise: pairing-generate ➜ block-<id> toggle ➜ simulate-request ➜ approve-<id>/deny-<id> ➜ page reload persistence.
Consider splitting /app/frontend/app/index.tsx (~91 dense lines but 7 components on single lines) into per-component files for maintainability — not blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: index.tsx addDevice() line 71: on error uses Alert.alert which is not visible in the Pairing modal on web preview. User gets no feedback that pairing-generate failed. Consider inline error state on the Pairing component.
index.tsx line 61 chains many awaits with early returns for d.error only; usage/requests fetch errors are silently swallowed. Add explicit error handling for u.error and r.error.

index.tsx line 68 realtime effect subscribes to extra_time_requests globally (no family filter possible since the table doesn't have family_id). This is fine but every parent will get all realtime events — filter client-side to family devices before load(true) to reduce noise.

AuthScreen submit() line 34: signup success message 'Cuenta creada' is shown even when the confirmation email flag toggles between projects; message states 'si la confirmación está activa' — that ambiguity is OK but consider auto-signing-in after signup when confirm-email is disabled (currently signUp doesn't yield a session and the user has to switch to login mode manually).

Loading text in the Pairing modal uses 'CÓDIGO DE EMPAREJAMIENTO' — spanish OK; the placeholder '------' should probably become 'Generando…' after pressing pairing-generate to give visual feedback while the insert is in flight.

rca_of_issue: Root cause: the schema drift on public.devices is only PARTIALLY resolved. In iteration_4 the missing NEW columns (name, profile_name, platform, online, blocked) were added via ALTER TABLE, which is what unblocked the SELECT PostgREST calls. But the LEGACY columns from the earlier partial migration (device_name text NOT NULL, device_type text NOT NULL CHECK, device_uuid text NOT NULL) were never dropped. The app's INSERT payload {family_id, name, profile_name, platform, pairing_code} therefore violates three NOT NULL constraints (Supabase returns 23502 one column at a time). pairing-generate silently fails (Alert.alert on web is not modal-scoped) and because index.tsx line 86 conditionally renders simulate-request only when devices.length>0, the entire extra_time_requests test surface becomes unreachable through the UI. Fix: drop the legacy columns (or DROP TABLE + recreate) and reload PostgREST schema cache. Long-term mitigation: make schema.sql column-idempotent and add inline error UI in the Pairing modal so silent 400s no longer masquerade as 'nothing happened'.
